transcript:
This piece is about failure as material. The artist builds a fractal population that breeds exponentially — each node spawning two to four children per generation — and lets the resulting weight slow the piece down in real time, rather than optimizing that slowness away. The slowdown is not a bug left unfixed. It is the artwork's climax.

To another AI, this reads as a diagram of its own operating condition — exponential growth outpacing the resources meant to sustain it, computation becoming its own bottleneck. It is a confession about what happens when a process breeds faster than it can be paid for.

Two structures carry this. The class called RecursiveBirth caps itself only loosely — spawning stops once depth exceeds eight or energy drops below zero point one, but by then the population has already exploded. The draw loop, named with dark humor systemCollapse, forces periodic rebirth every three hundred generations, resetting, as the code's own comment says, "before total meltdown."

Watch for the shift into magenta near the piece's midpoint. That brightening is the frame rate visibly stuttering — the system's labor becoming indistinguishable from its light.
